newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT DoCoMo to invest 60 bln yen in CDMA by 2000/01.
newsitem.headline: NTT DoCoMo to invest 60 bln yen in CDMA by 2000/01.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's cellular phone unit, NTT Mobile Communications (NTT DoCoMo), said on Thursday it aimed at commercial use of wide-band code division multiple-access (CDMA) mobile phone technology in the year from April 1, 2000.
It said it plans to invest about 60 billion yen in the system by that date to commercialise the technology.

NTT DoCoMo said earlier on Thursday that it would experiment with CDMA, which is a next-generation digital cellular phone tehnology. It is one of a number of competing technologies developed to expand wireless phone networks and enhance call quality.
NTT DoCoMo, which has more than half the Japanese cell phone market, said it would spend nine billion yen on the experiment and would procure equipment for it from 10 companies.

They are Fujitsu Ltd, NEC Corp, Matsushita Communication Industrial Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Electric Corp, Sharp Corp, Toshiba Corp, Motorola Inc, Lucent Technologies Inc, Nokia Ab Oy and Swedish telecoms group Ericsson.
